analysis.title: Will Anthropic pave the way for an AI rebound?
key_insights: Natixis frames the day as a tension between recovering AI sentiment, lifted by Anthropic's IPO pricing at $83 a share, and a risk-off undercurrent from elevated rates and a commodities selloff. US equity futures are higher this morning.
Asia diverged sharply overnight: Taiex -3%, Kospi -0.9%, HSI -2%. Natixis flags the gap between the US futures bid and China and the AI-exposed tech indices as worth watching.

The October FOMC minutes show a divided Fed that paused to gather information. Almost all participants judged further rate increases likely appropriate. Natixis says the minutes are somewhat stale, since a slightly above-expectations CPI print and more hawkish Fed comments have raised the risk of further tightening.
Treasuries rallied on Wednesday on solid demand at the 20-year auction. The 10Y closed near 5.05% with a modest bull flattening. Overnight the 10Y was 5.054% (-1.8bp) and the 30Y 5.399% (-1.4bp).
The dollar was the clear winner. DXY rose to 103.9, its highest since April 2025, and EUR/USD fell 0.53% to 1.096, a 19-month low.

The commodities selloff that began in September is accelerating. Copper fell on the LME as AI-linked bullish bets were unwound, gold fell below $3,800 (a 14-month low, -3%), and oil slipped below $93/bbl. The Bloomberg Commodity Index broke below its 200-day moving average for the first time since August 2025.

The rand fell to its lowest in almost a year (USD/ZAR +2% to 17.25), weighed down by the slump in gold. Bank Indonesia's surprise 25bp hike to 6% helped the rupiah resist the broader depreciation. The Australian dollar slid 0.8% to 0.6665 after a sharp miss on Australian jobs data.
European equities fell for a third straight session (Stoxx 600 -1.0%), led lower by miners at a 10-month low and the energy sector. The S&P 500 closed -0.2%.

UK October CPI rose to 3.6% YoY, in line with expectations and the highest in a year, driven by fuel and energy. Core CPI was 2.8% as expected and services inflation was 3.7% against a 3.8% forecast. Natixis assigns a 60% probability to a December BoE hike and expects at least two more, most likely in February and April 2027.

Euro area final October HICP was 4.0% YoY and 0.5% MoM, in line with the flash estimate, driven mainly by energy. Core was steady at 2.5%. A Natixis note says food prices have not driven this year's rise, but energy and adverse weather could add pressure.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83, above the $70-$78 range, and upsized to 980 million shares after reportedly drawing more than $500bn in orders. It raises $117.6bn if the 15% greenshoe is exercised, the largest IPO on record, at a valuation of about $1.5tn. It debuts on the Nasdaq today.

Carlyle's head of global credit says investors need not rush into AI data centers given the supply pipeline. He flags tenant concentration, weak business model visibility and tougher conditions for speculative developers, and is wary of chip-backed financing because decay value and technology risk are hard to underwrite.
Groupe Figaro announced a partnership with OpenAI after LVMH's media division did the same on Monday. Articles may appear in ChatGPT as summaries and excerpts with links.
Spain's People's Party, the frontrunner for the Nov. 29 election, says it would sell the state's roughly 18% CaixaBank stake, worth about €15bn. Natixis rates CaixaBank credit neutral.
Eurobank agreed to buy 65% of Bulgaria's Fibank for about €650mn in cash, valuing the target at €1bn. It triggers a mandatory tender offer, and Natixis rates it credit positive.
France's PLFSS social security financing bill passed the Senate 201 to 124. A joint committee is expected on 25 or 26 November.

market_movers.rationale: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 and debuts on the Nasdaq today. Natixis treats it as lifting AI sentiment and gives no rating or target.

earnings_insights: Zegona reported Q2-27 results (reported, not an estimate) with H1 EBITDAaL up 2% YoY. A €3.7bn debt refinancing should cut annual cost of debt by €60mn, and buybacks and dividends continue.
Iliad Group reported Q3-26 revenue of €2.74bn, up 5% quarter on quarter, with mobile subscribers up 0.2%. It kept its full-year equity free cash flow outlook of more than €1bn.

Golub Capital reported FY26 earnings that Natixis calls slightly negative. Q4-26 per-share earnings were materially lower YoY and NAV declined more, while distribution coverage stayed adequate and leverage was lower.

Oaktree reported FY26 earnings that Natixis calls slightly negative. Investment income and NAV were lower YoY and it booked a realized investment loss. The distribution was covered by adjusted NII and non-accruals were steady sequentially.

tension_points.bull_case: Anthropic's IPO priced at $83, above its range, on more than $500bn of reported orders, and US futures are bid this morning.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated rates, a divided Fed ready to keep hiking, a dollar at its highest since April 2025, and a commodities selloff that includes AI-linked copper bets being unwound. Asian tech fell sharply overnight.

tension_points.bull_case: Record IPO demand for Anthropic signals strong investor appetite for AI exposure.
tension_points.bear_case: Carlyle's head of global credit flags tenant concentration, weak business model visibility, supply that exceeds leasing demand, and hard-to-underwrite chip-backed financing.
